203	    """Frozen metrics for one scheme/parameter combination.
204	
205	    ``capacity`` is the number of messages one key pair can sign; ``elements``
206	    the number of 32-byte chain elements per (one-time) signature;
207	    ``sig_bytes`` and ``path_bytes`` the serialised signature and
208	    authentication-path sizes in bytes, excluding any leaf index and Python
209	    object overhead; ``steps`` the upper bound on hash-chain steps a verifier
210	    performs per (one-time) signature. ``w``/``height`` are ``None`` when the
211	    scheme does not use them.

214	    scheme: str
215	    w: int | None
216	    height: int | None
217	    capacity: int

224	def _wots_metrics(w: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
225	    """Return ``(n, steps)``: chain count and chain-step upper bound."""
226	    b, l1, l2 = _params(w)
227	    n = l1 + l2
228	    return n, n * (b - 1)

235	    8) only; ``merkle`` takes both (``height`` an integer from 1 to 8). An
236	    unknown scheme, a missing parameter or an unexpected one raises
237	    ``ValueError``.

241	            raise ValueError("lamport takes neither w nor height")
242	        return Params(
243	            scheme="lamport",
244	            w=None,
245	            height=None,
246	            capacity=1,
247	            elements=0,
248	            sig_bytes=256 * 32,
249	            path_bytes=0,
250	            steps=0,
251	        )

254	            raise ValueError("wots requires w")
255	        if height is not None:

312	def recommend_scheme(capacity: Any, budgets: Any, prefer: Any = "size") -> Params:
313	    """Return the :class:`Params` of the scheme best fitting capacity/budgets.
314	
315	    The cross-scheme counterpart of :func:`recommend`: instead of choosing
316	    only among Merkle configurations, enumerate every configuration
317	    :func:`profile` accepts — the two one-time schemes (Lamport, and W-OTS
318	    with ``w`` 4 and 8) and every Merkle configuration with ``w`` in
319	    ``(4, 8)`` times ``height`` from 1 to 8 — keep those whose ``capacity``
320	    covers the requested signature count and that satisfy both budgets, and
321	    rank the feasible set. The one-time candidates cover one signature and
322	    are present only when ``capacity == 1``; a request for more than one
323	    signature leaves the Merkle configurations as the only candidates.
324	
325	    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``budgets``
326	    must be a two-tuple, in order: an inclusive upper bound on one
327	    signature's serialised size (:attr:`Params.sig_bytes`) and on the
328	    verifier hash-chain step count (:attr:`Params.steps`). Each entry is
329	    either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive, non-boolean integer, and at
330	    least one entry must be set.
331	
332	    ``prefer="size"`` (the default) ranks candidates by ``sig_bytes`` first
333	    and ``steps`` second; ``prefer="speed"`` reverses the two. Both share
334	    the same ascending tie-break afterwards: spare capacity
335	    (candidate capacity minus the requested signature count), the scheme
336	    name lexicographically, then ``w`` and ``height``, with a missing
337	    parameter sorted ahead of any value. The first candidate after sorting
338	    is returned as a :class:`Params`.
339	
340	    Validation runs capacity first, budgets second and ``prefer`` last. A
341	    non-tuple ``budgets`` raises ``TypeError``; a boolean, non-integer or
342	    out-of-range ``capacity``, a wrong-length or otherwise illegal
343	    ``budgets`` tuple (including both entries ``None``), an unknown
344	    ``prefer`` value or the absence of any feasible candidate raises
345	    ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it draws no randomness, generates
346	    no keys and changes no state.
347	    """
348	    if (
349	        isinstance(capacity, bool)
350	        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
351	        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
352	    ):
353	        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
354	    if not isinstance(budgets, tuple):
355	        raise TypeError("budgets must be a 2-tuple of budget limits")
356	    if len(budgets) != 2:
357	        raise ValueError("budgets must contain exactly two entries")
358	
359	    labels = ("signature", "steps")
360	    limits = []
361	    for label, budget in zip(labels, budgets):
362	        if budget is None:
363	            limits.append(None)
364	        elif isinstance(budget, bool) or not isinstance(budget, int) or budget < 1:
365	            raise ValueError(f"{label} budget must be None or a positive integer")
366	        else:
367	            limits.append(budget)
368	    if all(limit is None for limit in limits):
369	        raise ValueError("at least one budget must be set")
370	    if prefer not in ("size", "speed"):
371	        raise ValueError('prefer must be "size" or "speed"')
372	    signature_limit, steps_limit = limits
373	
374	    candidates: list[Params] = []
375	    if capacity == 1:
376	        candidates.append(profile("lamport"))
377	        for w in (4, 8):
378	            candidates.append(profile("wots", w=w))
379	    for w in (4, 8):
380	        for height in range(1, 9):
381	            candidate = profile("merkle", w=w, height=height)
382	            if candidate.capacity >= capacity:
383	                candidates.append(candidate)
384	
385	    feasible = []
386	    for candidate in candidates:
387	        if signature_limit is not None and candidate.sig_bytes > signature_limit:
388	            continue
389	        if steps_limit is not None and candidate.steps > steps_limit:
390	            continue
391	        feasible.append(candidate)
392	    if not feasible:
393	        raise ValueError("no scheme fits the requested capacity and budgets")
394	
395	    def ranking(candidate: Params) -> tuple:
396	        tail = (
397	            candidate.capacity - capacity,
398	            candidate.scheme,
399	            candidate.w is not None,
400	            candidate.w,
401	            candidate.height is not None,
402	            candidate.height,
403	        )
404	        if prefer == "speed":
405	            return (candidate.steps, candidate.sig_bytes) + tail
406	        return (candidate.sig_bytes, candidate.steps) + tail
407	
408	    return min(feasible, key=ranking)

546	def merkle_deployment_frontier(
547	    capacity: Any, budgets: Any
548	) -> tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, ...]:
549	    """Return every feasible, non-dominated ordinary Merkle deployment as a tuple.
550	
551	    Where :func:`recommend_merkle_deployment` ranks the feasible configs and
552	    returns one, this function keeps the whole Pareto frontier so a caller can
553	    inspect the trade-off between storage, signature, proof and verification
554	    costs: it enumerates every Merkle candidate — ``w`` in ``(4, 8)`` times
555	    ``height`` from 1 to 8 — whose ``leaf_count`` covers ``capacity``, keeps
556	    those satisfying every set budget, reusing
557	    :func:`merkle_storage_profile` for the wire sizes and
558	    :func:`profile` for the per-signature verifier hash-chain step count, and
559	    drops every dominated candidate.
560	
561	    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``budgets``
562	    must be a four-tuple, in order: an upper bound on the checkpoint bytes
563	    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.checkpoint_bytes`), on one signature wire
564	    length (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.signature_wire_bytes`), on one
565	    standalone proof wire length
566	    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.proof_wire_bytes`) and on the per-signature
567	    verifier hash-chain step count (``profile("merkle", ...)``'s ``steps``).
568	    Each entry is either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive, non-boolean
569	    integer, and at least one entry must be set; every bound is inclusive.
570	
571	    A feasible profile *A* dominates another feasible profile *B* when
572	    ``A`` is no greater than ``B`` on all four metrics — checkpoint bytes,
573	    signature wire bytes, proof wire bytes and verifier steps — and strictly
574	    smaller on at least one; every dominated candidate is dropped and the
575	    survivors are deduplicated by value. No preference is applied, so a
576	    configuration trading speed for size (or the reverse) is never discarded
577	    ahead of the dominance test. The returned tuple is sorted stably and
578	    ascending by verifier steps, signature wire bytes, proof wire bytes,
579	    checkpoint bytes, leaf count, ``w`` and ``height``.
580	
581	    A non-tuple ``budgets`` raises ``TypeError``; a wrong-length or otherwise
582	    illegal ``budgets`` tuple, an out-of-range ``capacity`` or the absence of
583	    any feasible candidate raises ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it
584	    draws no randomness, generates no keys and changes no state.
585	    """
586	    limits = _validate_deployment_budgets(budgets)
587	    if (
588	        isinstance(capacity, bool)
589	        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
590	        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
591	    ):
592	        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
593	    checkpoint_limit, signature_limit, proof_limit, steps_limit = limits
594	
595	    candidates: list[tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int]] = []
596	    for w in (4, 8):
597	        for height in range(1, 9):
598	            storage = merkle_storage_profile(w, height)
599	            if storage.leaf_count < capacity:
600	                continue
601	            if checkpoint_limit is not None and storage.checkpoint_bytes > checkpoint_limit:
602	                continue
603	            if signature_limit is not None and storage.signature_wire_bytes > signature_limit:
604	                continue
605	            if proof_limit is not None and storage.proof_wire_bytes > proof_limit:
606	                continue
607	            steps = profile("merkle", w=w, height=height).steps
608	            if steps_limit is not None and steps > steps_limit:
609	                continue
610	            candidates.append((storage, steps))
611	    if not candidates:
612	        raise ValueError("no Merkle configuration fits the requested capacity and budgets")
613	
614	    def dominates(
615	        a: tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int],
616	        b: tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int],
617	    ) -> bool:
618	        a_storage, a_steps = a
619	        b_storage, b_steps = b
620	        no_worse = (
621	            a_storage.checkpoint_bytes <= b_storage.checkpoint_bytes
622	            and a_storage.signature_wire_bytes <= b_storage.signature_wire_bytes
623	            and a_storage.proof_wire_bytes <= b_storage.proof_wire_bytes
624	            and a_steps <= b_steps
625	        )
626	        strictly_better = (
627	            a_storage.checkpoint_bytes < b_storage.checkpoint_bytes
628	            or a_storage.signature_wire_bytes < b_storage.signature_wire_bytes
629	            or a_storage.proof_wire_bytes < b_storage.proof_wire_bytes
630	            or a_steps < b_steps
631	        )
632	        return no_worse and strictly_better
633	
634	    non_dominated = [
635	        candidate
636	        for candidate in candidates
637	        if not any(dominates(other, candidate) for other in candidates)
638	    ]
639	
640	    unique: list[MerkleStorageProfile] = []
641	    seen: set[MerkleStorageProfile] = set()
642	    for storage, _steps in non_dominated:
643	        if storage not in seen:
644	            seen.add(storage)
645	            unique.append(storage)
646	
647	    unique.sort(
648	        key=lambda storage: (
649	            profile("merkle", w=storage.w, height=storage.height).steps,
650	            storage.signature_wire_bytes,
651	            storage.proof_wire_bytes,
652	            storage.checkpoint_bytes,
653	            storage.leaf_count,
654	            storage.w,
655	            storage.height,
656	        )
657	    )
658	    return tuple(unique)
659

679	def recommend_merkle_deployment_weighted(
680	    capacity: Any,
681	    budgets: Any,
682	    weights: Any,
683	) -> MerkleStorageProfile:
684	    """Pick one non-dominated Merkle deployment by weighted normalised costs.
685	
686	    Computes :func:`merkle_deployment_frontier` exactly once and ranks the
687	    returned feasible, non-dominated ordinary Merkle deployments by a
688	    caller-supplied linear score over four costs: the checkpoint bytes
689	    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.checkpoint_bytes`), one signature wire
690	    length (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.signature_wire_bytes`), one
691	    standalone proof wire length
692	    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.proof_wire_bytes`) and the per-signature
693	    verifier hash-chain step count (``profile("merkle", ...)``'s
694	    ``steps``).
695	
696	    ``weights`` must be a four-tuple in that same order — checkpoint bytes,
697	    signature wire bytes, standalone proof wire bytes and per-signature
698	    chain steps. Every weight must be a non-boolean, non-negative integer
699	    and at least one must be positive. Each of the four costs is min-max
700	    normalised over the whole frontier as ``(x - min) / (max - min)``, with
701	    a zero span scoring ``0``; the weighted score is the sum of the four
702	    normalised costs times their weights, divided by the weight total, all
703	    compared as exact rationals (``fractions.Fraction``) with no floating
704	    point anywhere. The survivor with the smallest score is returned; equal
705	    scores are broken ascending by checkpoint bytes, leaf count, ``w`` and
706	    ``height``. The candidate enumeration and Pareto filtering are not
707	    duplicated: the frontier is the only source of candidates and is called
708	    exactly once.
709	
710	    ``capacity`` and the four-tuple ``budgets`` follow
711	    :func:`merkle_deployment_frontier`'s types, ranges, inclusive-budget,
712	    exception and no-feasible-candidate rules exactly, so a violation
713	    raises exactly as that function does (and is screened before
714	    ``weights``). A non-tuple ``weights`` or a non-integer member raises
715	    ``TypeError``; a wrong-length tuple or a boolean, negative or all-zero
716	    weight raises ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it draws no
717	    randomness, generates no keys and changes no state.
718	    """
719	    frontier = merkle_deployment_frontier(capacity, budgets)
720	    validated_weights = _validate_deployment_weights(weights)
721	
722	    def metrics(storage: MerkleStorageProfile) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
723	        return (
724	            storage.checkpoint_bytes,
725	            storage.signature_wire_bytes,
726	            storage.proof_wire_bytes,
727	            profile("merkle", w=storage.w, height=storage.height).steps,
728	        )
729	
730	    metric_rows = tuple(metrics(storage) for storage in frontier)
731	    spans = tuple(
732	        (min(row[i] for row in metric_rows), max(row[i] for row in metric_rows))
733	        for i in range(4)
734	    )
735	    weight_total = sum(validated_weights)
736	
737	    def ranking(
738	        storage: MerkleStorageProfile,
739	    ) -> tuple[Fraction, int, int, int, int]:
740	        score = Fraction(0)
741	        for value, weight, (low, high) in zip(metrics(storage), validated_weights, spans):
742	            if high > low:
743	                score += weight * Fraction(value - low, high - low)
744	        score /= weight_total
745	        return (
746	            score,
747	            storage.checkpoint_bytes,
748	            storage.leaf_count,
749	            storage.w,
750	            storage.height,
751	        )
752	
753	    return min(frontier, key=ranking)
754

810	    one weight of each scenario must be positive; repeated scenarios are
811	    counted separately.

814	    source of candidates — the candidate enumeration and Pareto filtering
815	    are not duplicated. Each of the four costs is min-max normalised over
816	    the whole frontier as ``(x - min) / (max - min)``, with a zero span
817	    scoring ``0``. For each scenario, a candidate's score is the weighted
818	    sum of its four normalised costs divided by the scenario's weight
819	    total, all compared as exact rationals (``fractions.Fraction``) with no
820	    floating point anywhere. Each scenario's own minimum score is then
821	    subtracted from every candidate's score to give that scenario's
822	    regret; deployments are ranked first by the greatest regret over the
823	    scenarios (the minimax-regret choice), then by the sum of the
824	    regrets, then by the tuple of per-scenario scores, all ascending. A
825	    complete tie is broken ascending by checkpoint bytes, leaf count,
826	    ``w`` and ``height``, and the first survivor is returned as a
827	    :class:`MerkleStorageProfile`.
828	
829	    ``capacity`` and the four-tuple ``budgets`` follow
830	    :func:`merkle_deployment_frontier`'s types, ranges, inclusive-budget,
831	    exception and no-feasible-candidate rules exactly, so a violation
832	    raises exactly as that function does (and is screened before
833	    ``scenarios``). A non-tuple ``scenarios`` or scenario member, or a
834	    non-integer weight, raises ``TypeError``; an empty scenario tuple, a
835	    wrong-length scenario, or a boolean, negative or all-zero weight
836	    raises ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it draws no randomness,
837	    generates no keys and changes no state.
838	    """
839	    frontier = merkle_deployment_frontier(capacity, budgets)
840	    validated_scenarios = _validate_deployment_weight_scenarios(scenarios)
841	
842	    def metrics(storage: MerkleStorageProfile) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
843	        return (
844	            storage.checkpoint_bytes,
845	            storage.signature_wire_bytes,
846	            storage.proof_wire_bytes,
847	            profile("merkle", w=storage.w, height=storage.height).steps,
848	        )
849	
850	    metric_rows = tuple(metrics(storage) for storage in frontier)
851	    spans = tuple(
852	        (min(row[i] for row in metric_rows), max(row[i] for row in metric_rows))
853	        for i in range(4)
854	    )
855	
856	    def normalised(row: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[Fraction, ...]:
857	        return tuple(
858	            Fraction(value - low, high - low) if high > low else Fraction(0)
859	            for value, (low, high) in zip(row, spans)
860	        )
861	
862	    normalised_rows = tuple(normalised(row) for row in metric_rows)
863	    scenario_totals = tuple(sum(weights) for weights in validated_scenarios)
864	
865	    def scenario_scores(row: tuple[Fraction, ...]) -> tuple[Fraction, ...]:
866	        return tuple(
867	            sum(
868	                (weight * component for weight, component in zip(weights, row)),
869	                Fraction(0),
870	            )
871	            / weight_total
872	            for weights, weight_total in zip(validated_scenarios, scenario_totals)
873	        )
874	
875	    score_rows = tuple(scenario_scores(row) for row in normalised_rows)
876	    scenario_best = tuple(
877	        min(row[scenario_index] for row in score_rows)
878	        for scenario_index in range(len(validated_scenarios))
879	    )
880	
881	    def ranking(
882	        entry: tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, tuple[Fraction, ...]],
883	    ) -> tuple[Fraction, Fraction, tuple[Fraction, ...], int, int, int, int]:
884	        storage, scores = entry
885	        regrets = tuple(
886	            score - best for score, best in zip(scores, scenario_best)
887	        )
888	        return (
889	            max(regrets),
890	            sum(regrets, Fraction(0)),

892	            storage.checkpoint_bytes,
893	            storage.leaf_count,
894	            storage.w,
895	            storage.height,

1114	    (``16 + 32 * (n + height)``) and ``m`` the canonical multi-proof node
1115	    count — siblings outside the current index set at each level, with the
1116	    set shifted right and deduplicated between levels — the result is
1117	    ``(m, 58 + k * (4 + S), 60 + k * (4 + 32 * n) + 35 * m)``: the carried

1119	    length of a :func:`multiproof_encode` blob. The estimate is pure: no

"""Static parameter analysis for pqattest schemes.

:func:`profile` reports the size and cost metrics of a scheme/parameter
combination without generating any keys, and :func:`recommend` picks a Merkle
configuration for a desired signature capacity, :func:`recommend_merkle_deployment`
picks one that additionally fits deployment budgets. :func:`merkle_storage_profile`
breaks the Merkle wire sizes down per serialised object and
:func:`merkle_transport_profile` sizes a batch or multi-proof over a chosen
leaf-index set. :func:`recommend_merkle_transport_deployment` chooses both the
tree parameters and the transport encoding together under checkpoint, batch,
multi-proof and verifier-step budgets, and
:func:`merkle_transport_deployment_frontier` returns every feasible,
non-dominated choice of the same joint deployment as a tuple instead of
ranking one. :func:`recommend_merkle_transport_deployment_weighted` ranks
that same frontier by a caller-supplied five-tuple of non-negative weights
over its five min-max-normalised costs — batch-proof bytes, multi-proof
bytes, carried nodes, checkpoint bytes and verifier steps — with exact
:class:`fractions.Fraction` arithmetic, and returns one profile.
:func:`recommend_merkle_transport_deployment_weighted_scenarios` ranks that
same joint-deployment frontier against several such weight scenarios at
once, minimising the worst per-scenario regret (then regret sum, then
per-scenario scores) with the same exact :class:`fractions.Fraction`
arithmetic, and returns one profile.
:func:`recommend_merkle_transport_workload`
extends that joint choice to several independent leaf-index groups, each carried
in its own transport, under checkpoint, per-group, aggregate and verifier-step
budgets. :func:`merkle_transport_workload_frontier` returns every feasible,
non-dominated choice of the same workload as a tuple instead of ranking one.
:func:`recommend_merkle_transport_workload_weighted` ranks that same
frontier by a caller-supplied four-tuple of non-negative weights over its
four min-max-normalised costs in the order checkpoint bytes, single-group
peak, aggregate transport and verifier steps (the weighted sum divided by
the weight total), with exact :class:`fractions.Fraction` arithmetic, and
returns one profile.
:func:`recommend_merkle_transport_workload_weighted_scenarios` ranks that
same workload frontier against several such weight scenarios at once,
minimising the worst per-scenario regret (then regret sum, then
per-scenario scores) with the same exact :class:`fractions.Fraction`
arithmetic, and returns one profile.
:func:`merkle_mode_frontier` goes further and enumerates every per-group
``batch``/``multiproof`` mode combination of the workload under checkpoint,
per-group, aggregate, verifier-step and carried-node budgets, returning the
feasible, non-dominated mode choices as a tuple.
:func:`recommend_merkle_mode_deployment` ranks that mode frontier by a
business preference — ``"compact"``, ``"nodes"`` or ``"speed"`` — and
returns one profile.
:func:`recommend_merkle_mode_weighted` instead ranks that same mode frontier
by a caller-supplied five-tuple of non-negative weights over its five
min-max-normalised costs in the order checkpoint bytes, single-group peak,
aggregate transport, verifier steps and carried nodes (the weighted sum
divided by the weight total), with exact :class:`fractions.Fraction`
arithmetic, and returns one profile.
:func:`recommend_merkle_mode_weighted_scenarios` instead ranks that same
mode frontier against several five-tuples of non-negative cost weights at
once — checkpoint bytes, single-group peak, aggregate transport, verifier
steps and carried nodes — minimising the worst per-scenario regret (then
regret sum, then per-scenario scores) with the same exact
:class:`fractions.Fraction` arithmetic, and returns one profile.
:func:`merkle_deployment_frontier` likewise returns the whole Pareto frontier
of ordinary Merkle deployments under checkpoint, signature, proof and
verifier-step budgets. :func:`recommend_merkle_deployment_weighted` ranks
that same ordinary-deployment frontier by a caller-supplied four-tuple of
non-negative weights over its four min-max-normalised costs in the order
checkpoint bytes, signature wire length, standalone proof wire length and
verifier steps (the weighted sum divided by the weight total), with exact
:class:`fractions.Fraction` arithmetic, and returns one profile.
:func:`recommend_merkle_deployment_weighted_scenarios` ranks that same
ordinary-deployment frontier against several such four-weight scenarios
at once — checkpoint bytes, signature wire length, standalone proof wire
length and verifier steps — minimising the worst per-scenario regret
(then regret sum, then per-scenario scores) with the same exact
:class:`fractions.Fraction` arithmetic, and returns one profile.
:func:`explain_merkle_deployment_weighted` exports the decision-cost
breakdown behind that same weighted ranking as a tuple of frozen
:class:`MerkleDeploymentScore` rows — one per frontier member, in
frontier order, each carrying the candidate's config, its four
normalised costs, its final score and a selected flag — with the same
exact :class:`fractions.Fraction` arithmetic.
:func:`merkle_verify_profile` compares the
verifier-side SHA-256 hash cost of a batch proof against a multi-proof over
the same leaf set, returning a :class:`MerkleVerifyProfile`.
:func:`merkle_verify_workload_profile` extends that comparison to several
independent leaf-index groups, each carried in its own ``"batch"`` or
``"multiproof"`` transport, and totals the per-group SHA-256 work in a
:class:`MerkleVerifyWorkloadProfile`. :func:`merkle_verify_mode_frontier`
joins the two: it enumerates every per-group mode combination of every
candidate config under checkpoint, per-group peak, aggregate transport,
verifier-step, carried-node and verifier-hash budgets, returning the
feasible, non-dominated choices as frozen :class:`MerkleModeCost` tuples.
:func:`merkle_cardinality_frontier` is the worst-case-position counterpart
for workloads where only each group's leaf count is fixed: every
multi-proof group is billed at the maximum transport bytes, canonical node
count and internal-node hash count over every same-size strictly
increasing index subset of the candidate tree, and it returns the same
feasible, non-dominated :class:`MerkleModeCost` frontier.
:func:`recommend_merkle_cardinality_deployment` ranks that cardinality
frontier by one of five preferences — ``"compact"``, ``"verify"``,
``"nodes"``, ``"speed"`` or ``"robust"`` — and returns one
:class:`MerkleModeCost`.
:func:`recommend_merkle_cardinality_weighted` ranks the same frontier by a
caller-supplied five-tuple of non-negative weights over its five
min-max-normalised costs, all arithmetic exact via :class:`fractions.Fraction`,
and returns one :class:`MerkleModeCost`.
:func:`explain_merkle_cardinality_weighted` exports the decision-cost
breakdown behind that same weighted cardinality ranking as a tuple of frozen
:class:`MerkleCardinalityScore` rows — one per frontier member, in frontier
order, each carrying the candidate's plan/cost pairing, its five normalised
costs, its final score and a selected flag — with the same exact
:class:`fractions.Fraction` arithmetic.
:func:`recommend_merkle_verify_mode_weighted` ranks the fixed-position
:func:`merkle_verify_mode_frontier` frontier against several weight scenarios
at once, minimising the worst per-scenario regret (then regret sum, then
per-scenario scores) with the same exact :class:`fractions.Fraction`
arithmetic, and returns one :class:`MerkleModeCost`.
:func:`recommend_merkle_cardinality_weighted_scenarios` applies that same
preference-drift-robust multi-scenario minimax-regret ranking to the
worst-case-position :func:`merkle_cardinality_frontier` frontier.
:func:`recommend_merkle_verify_mode_deployment` ranks the fixed-position
:func:`merkle_verify_mode_frontier` frontier by one of five business
preferences — ``"compact"``, ``"verify"``, ``"nodes"``, ``"speed"`` or
``"robust"`` — and returns one :class:`MerkleModeCost`.
:func:`recommend_merkle_verify_mode_deployment_weighted` ranks that same
fixed-position frontier by a caller-supplied five-tuple of non-negative
weights over its five min-max-normalised costs (total transport,
single-group peak, total verifier hashes, carried nodes and per-signature
chain steps), the weighted sum divided by the weight total with exact
:class:`fractions.Fraction` arithmetic, and returns one
:class:`MerkleModeCost`.
:func:`recommend_scheme` is the cross-scheme selector: it enumerates every
configuration :func:`profile` accepts — the two one-time schemes and both
Merkle ``w`` choices at every tree height — keeps those covering the
requested signature count and fitting a two-tuple of signature-size and
chain-step budgets, and ranks the feasible set by a ``"size"`` or
``"speed"`` preference, returning one :class:`Params`.
All thirty-three
are pure functions: no randomness, no
state, no I/O, no keys are generated.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from fractions import Fraction
from itertools import product
from typing import Any

from .merkle import _canonical_multiproof_nodes, _validate_height
from .wots import ELEMENT_BYTES, _params, _validate_w

__all__ = [
    "Params",
    "MerkleStorageProfile",
    "MerkleDeploymentScore",
    "MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile",
    "MerkleTransportWorkloadProfile",
    "MerkleModeCost",
    "MerkleVerifyProfile",
    "MerkleVerifyWorkloadProfile",
    "MerkleVerifyModeScore",
    "MerkleCardinalityScore",
    "profile",
    "recommend",
    "recommend_scheme",
    "recommend_merkle_deployment",
    "merkle_deployment_frontier",
    "recommend_merkle_deployment_weighted",
    "recommend_merkle_deployment_weighted_scenarios",
    "explain_merkle_deployment_weighted",
    "explain_merkle_cardinality_weighted",
    "recommend_merkle_transport_deployment",
    "merkle_transport_deployment_frontier",
    "recommend_merkle_transport_deployment_weighted",
    "recommend_merkle_transport_deployment_weighted_scenarios",
    "recommend_merkle_transport_workload",
    "merkle_transport_workload_frontier",
    "recommend_merkle_transport_workload_weighted",
    "recommend_merkle_transport_workload_weighted_scenarios",
    "merkle_mode_frontier",
    "merkle_verify_mode_frontier",
    "merkle_cardinality_frontier",
    "recommend_merkle_cardinality_deployment",
    "recommend_merkle_cardinality_weighted",
    "recommend_merkle_cardinality_weighted_scenarios",
    "recommend_merkle_verify_mode_deployment",
    "recommend_merkle_verify_mode_deployment_weighted",

_SCHEMES = ("lamport", "wots", "merkle")
_MAX_CAPACITY = 256


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Params:
    """Frozen metrics for one scheme/parameter combination.

    ``capacity`` is the number of messages one key pair can sign; ``elements``
    the number of 32-byte chain elements per (one-time) signature;
    ``sig_bytes`` and ``path_bytes`` the serialised signature and
    authentication-path sizes in bytes, excluding any leaf index and Python
    object overhead; ``steps`` the upper bound on hash-chain steps a verifier
    performs per (one-time) signature. ``w``/``height`` are ``None`` when the
    scheme does not use them.
    """

    scheme: str
    w: int | None
    height: int | None
    capacity: int
    elements: int
    sig_bytes: int
    path_bytes: int
    steps: int


def _wots_metrics(w: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Return ``(n, steps)``: chain count and chain-step upper bound."""
    b, l1, l2 = _params(w)
    n = l1 + l2
    return n, n * (b - 1)


def profile(scheme: str, w: Any = None, height: Any = None) -> Params:
    """Return the :class:`Params` metrics for a scheme configuration.

    ``lamport`` takes neither ``w`` nor ``height``; ``wots`` takes ``w`` (4 or
    8) only; ``merkle`` takes both (``height`` an integer from 1 to 8). An
    unknown scheme, a missing parameter or an unexpected one raises
    ``ValueError``.
    """
    if scheme == "lamport":
        if w is not None or height is not None:
            raise ValueError("lamport takes neither w nor height")
        return Params(
            scheme="lamport",
            w=None,
            height=None,
            capacity=1,
            elements=0,
            sig_bytes=256 * 32,
            path_bytes=0,
            steps=0,
        )
    if scheme == "wots":
        if w is None:
            raise ValueError("wots requires w")
        if height is not None:
            raise ValueError("wots takes no height")
        w = _validate_w(w)
        n, steps = _wots_metrics(w)
        return Params(
            scheme="wots",
            w=w,
            height=None,
            capacity=1,
            elements=n,
            sig_bytes=n * ELEMENT_BYTES,
            path_bytes=0,
            steps=steps,
        )
    if scheme == "merkle":
        if w is None or height is None:
            raise ValueError("merkle requires both w and height")
        w = _validate_w(w)
        height = _validate_height(height)
        n, steps = _wots_metrics(w)
        return Params(
            scheme="merkle",
            w=w,
            height=height,
            capacity=1 << height,
            elements=n,
            sig_bytes=(n + height) * ELEMENT_BYTES,
            path_bytes=height * ELEMENT_BYTES,
            steps=steps,
        )
    raise ValueError(f"unknown scheme: {scheme!r}")


def recommend(capacity: Any, prefer: str = "size") -> Params:
    """Return the Merkle :class:`Params` covering ``capacity`` signatures.

    ``capacity`` must be an integer from 1 to 256 (non-bool); the height is
    the smallest one with ``2 ** height >= capacity`` and at least 1.
    ``prefer="size"`` picks ``w=8`` (shorter signatures), ``prefer="speed"``
    picks ``w=4`` (fewer chain steps). Anything else raises ``ValueError``.
    """
    if (
        isinstance(capacity, bool)
        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
    ):
        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
    if prefer == "size":
        w = 8
    elif prefer == "speed":
        w = 4
    else:
        raise ValueError('prefer must be "size" or "speed"')
    height = max(1, (capacity - 1).bit_length())
    return profile("merkle", w=w, height=height)


def recommend_scheme(capacity: Any, budgets: Any, prefer: Any = "size") -> Params:
    """Return the :class:`Params` of the scheme best fitting capacity/budgets.

    The cross-scheme counterpart of :func:`recommend`: instead of choosing
    only among Merkle configurations, enumerate every configuration
    :func:`profile` accepts — the two one-time schemes (Lamport, and W-OTS
    with ``w`` 4 and 8) and every Merkle configuration with ``w`` in
    ``(4, 8)`` times ``height`` from 1 to 8 — keep those whose ``capacity``
    covers the requested signature count and that satisfy both budgets, and
    rank the feasible set. The one-time candidates cover one signature and
    are present only when ``capacity == 1``; a request for more than one
    signature leaves the Merkle configurations as the only candidates.

    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``budgets``
    must be a two-tuple, in order: an inclusive upper bound on one
    signature's serialised size (:attr:`Params.sig_bytes`) and on the
    verifier hash-chain step count (:attr:`Params.steps`). Each entry is
    either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive, non-boolean integer, and at
    least one entry must be set.

    ``prefer="size"`` (the default) ranks candidates by ``sig_bytes`` first
    and ``steps`` second; ``prefer="speed"`` reverses the two. Both share
    the same ascending tie-break afterwards: spare capacity
    (candidate capacity minus the requested signature count), the scheme
    name lexicographically, then ``w`` and ``height``, with a missing
    parameter sorted ahead of any value. The first candidate after sorting
    is returned as a :class:`Params`.

    Validation runs capacity first, budgets second and ``prefer`` last. A
    non-tuple ``budgets`` raises ``TypeError``; a boolean, non-integer or
    out-of-range ``capacity``, a wrong-length or otherwise illegal
    ``budgets`` tuple (including both entries ``None``), an unknown
    ``prefer`` value or the absence of any feasible candidate raises
    ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it draws no randomness, generates
    no keys and changes no state.
    """
    if (
        isinstance(capacity, bool)
        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
    ):
        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
    if not isinstance(budgets, tuple):
        raise TypeError("budgets must be a 2-tuple of budget limits")
    if len(budgets) != 2:
        raise ValueError("budgets must contain exactly two entries")

    labels = ("signature", "steps")
    limits = []
    for label, budget in zip(labels, budgets):
        if budget is None:
            limits.append(None)
        elif isinstance(budget, bool) or not isinstance(budget, int) or budget < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{label} budget must be None or a positive integer")
        else:
            limits.append(budget)
    if all(limit is None for limit in limits):
        raise ValueError("at least one budget must be set")
    if prefer not in ("size", "speed"):
        raise ValueError('prefer must be "size" or "speed"')
    signature_limit, steps_limit = limits

    candidates: list[Params] = []
    if capacity == 1:
        candidates.append(profile("lamport"))
        for w in (4, 8):
            candidates.append(profile("wots", w=w))
    for w in (4, 8):
        for height in range(1, 9):
            candidate = profile("merkle", w=w, height=height)
            if candidate.capacity >= capacity:
                candidates.append(candidate)

    feasible = []
    for candidate in candidates:
        if signature_limit is not None and candidate.sig_bytes > signature_limit:
            continue
        if steps_limit is not None and candidate.steps > steps_limit:
            continue
        feasible.append(candidate)
    if not feasible:
        raise ValueError("no scheme fits the requested capacity and budgets")

    def ranking(candidate: Params) -> tuple:
        tail = (
            candidate.capacity - capacity,
            candidate.scheme,
            candidate.w is not None,
            candidate.w,
            candidate.height is not None,
            candidate.height,
        )
        if prefer == "speed":
            return (candidate.steps, candidate.sig_bytes) + tail
        return (candidate.sig_bytes, candidate.steps) + tail

    return min(feasible, key=ranking)


def recommend_merkle_deployment(
    capacity: Any, budgets: Any, prefer: Any = "size"
) -> MerkleStorageProfile:
    """Return the :class:`MerkleStorageProfile` fitting deployment budgets.

    Unlike :func:`recommend`, which only minimises the tree height, this
    enumerates every Merkle candidate — ``w`` in ``(4, 8)`` times ``height``
    from 1 to 8 — keeps those whose ``leaf_count`` covers ``capacity`` and
    that satisfy every set budget, and ranks the feasible set.

    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``budgets``
    must be a four-tuple, in order: an upper bound on the checkpoint bytes
    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.checkpoint_bytes`), on one signature wire
    length (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.signature_wire_bytes`), on one
    standalone proof wire length (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.proof_wire_bytes`)
    and on the verifier hash-chain step count (``profile("merkle", ...)``'s
    ``steps``). Each entry is either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive,
    non-boolean integer, and at least one entry must be set.

    ``prefer="size"`` ranks candidates lexicographically by signature wire
    length, proof wire length, checkpoint bytes, steps, leaf count, ``w`` and
    ``height``; ``prefer="speed"`` minimises steps first and then applies the
    same remaining order. The first candidate after sorting is returned as a
    :class:`MerkleStorageProfile`.

    A non-tuple ``budgets`` raises ``TypeError``; a tuple of the wrong length,
    an illegal member, an out-of-range ``capacity``, an unknown ``prefer``
    value or the absence of any feasible candidate raises ``ValueError``. The
    function is pure: it draws no randomness, generates no keys and changes
    no state.
    """
    if not isinstance(budgets, tuple):
        raise TypeError("budgets must be a 4-tuple of budget limits")
    if len(budgets) != 4:
        raise ValueError("budgets must contain exactly four entries")
    if (
        isinstance(capacity, bool)
        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
    ):
        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
    if prefer not in ("size", "speed"):
        raise ValueError('prefer must be "size" or "speed"')

    labels = ("checkpoint", "signature", "proof", "steps")
    limits = []
    for label, budget in zip(labels, budgets):
        if budget is None:
            limits.append(None)
        elif isinstance(budget, bool) or not isinstance(budget, int) or budget < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{label} budget must be None or a positive integer")
        else:
            limits.append(budget)
    if all(limit is None for limit in limits):
        raise ValueError("at least one budget must be set")
    checkpoint_limit, signature_limit, proof_limit, steps_limit = limits

    feasible = []
    for w in (4, 8):
        for height in range(1, 9):
            storage = merkle_storage_profile(w, height)
            if storage.leaf_count < capacity:
                continue
            if checkpoint_limit is not None and storage.checkpoint_bytes > checkpoint_limit:
                continue
            if signature_limit is not None and storage.signature_wire_bytes > signature_limit:
                continue
            if proof_limit is not None and storage.proof_wire_bytes > proof_limit:
                continue
            steps = profile("merkle", w=w, height=height).steps
            if steps_limit is not None and steps > steps_limit:
                continue
            feasible.append((storage, steps))
    if not feasible:
        raise ValueError("no Merkle configuration fits the requested capacity and budgets")

    def ranking(candidate: tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int]) -> tuple[int, ...]:
        storage, steps = candidate
        ordered = (
            storage.signature_wire_bytes,
            storage.proof_wire_bytes,
            storage.checkpoint_bytes,
            steps,
            storage.leaf_count,
            storage.w,
            storage.height,
        )
        if prefer == "speed":
            return (steps,) + ordered
        return ordered

    feasible.sort(key=ranking)
    return feasible[0][0]
